comparison: Perfect agreement on FOXC2 marking quiescent SSCs (C2, C25-C35). Both evaluations find the multi-modal evidence (scRNA-seq, immunofluorescence, pseudotime analysis) strongly supportive. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding as 'solid' and note the quiescent nature of FOXC2+ cells.

Perfect agreement on lineage tracing demonstrating FOXC2+ cells as bona fide SSCs (C3, C36-C46, C83-C84). Both evaluations emphasize the compelling nature of the temporal progression data, transplantation assays, and offspring generation. Peer reviewers describe experiments as 'well-designed' with 'interesting results.'

Perfect agreement on genetic ablation experiments (C4, C47, C49-C51). Both evaluations find strong evidence that FOXC2+ cell ablation leads to uSPG pool depletion. Peer reviewers affirm the conclusion is 'supported by the data presented.'

Perfect agreement on chemoresistance and regenerative capacity (C5, C52-C60, C92-C96). Both evaluations highlight the busulfan treatment data showing FOXC2+ cell survival and subsequent regeneration. Peer reviewers explicitly support the finding with detailed description of the temporal dynamics.

Strong agreement on FOXC2 requirement for adult SSC maintenance (C6, C61-C65). OpenEval includes C103 (lack of early phenotype) while peer review addresses this separately in R8. Both evaluations emphasize the progressive, age-dependent phenotype leading to infertility.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic findings (C7, C66-C82, C89). Both evaluations find the CUT&Tag and scRNA-seq data strongly support FOXC2's role in cell cycle regulation and quiescence maintenance. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the mechanistic link to mitotic cell cycle inhibition.

Strong agreement on overall model (C8, C97-C102). Both evaluations support the synthesis of findings into a coherent SSC model. OpenEval notes C98 involves speculation requiring validation; peer reviewers accept the overall conclusions as 'convincing' and 'solid.'

Agreement on human translational relevance (C105-C107). Both evaluations accept the human expression data. OpenEval explicitly notes functional conservation (C107) remains speculative without functional experiments, while peer reviewers implicitly accept translational significance without detailed critique.

Agreement on speculative nature of C87. Both evaluations recognize this claim about FOXC2+ cells as a reservoir requires further validation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN; peer review notes it as speculation requiring validation through multiple lineage tracing and live imaging.

Partial overlap on C103 (lack of early knockout phenotype). OpenEval includes this in R5 as supporting evidence for adult-specific role. Peer review R8 implicitly accepts this observation by noting progressive phenotype beginning at 2 months.

Partial overlap on contextual claims C85-C86. OpenEval groups these as supported contextual observations. Peer review R10 addresses C85-C87 together, with C85-C86 accepted as context and C87 marked as speculation.

Minimal overlap on C104 (citation-based contextual claim). OpenEval includes this in a group of supported contextual observations. Peer review R8 does not explicitly address this claim but accepts related contextual information.

OpenEval R10 addresses background and literature context claims (C1, C9-C24, C108). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than systematically evaluating background claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses C88 (quantitative observation on FOXC2+/MKI67+ overlap). No separate peer review evaluation found for this specific quantitative detail, though it supports findings discussed in peer R1.
